profile.entities: Jana Small Finance Bank Ltd. Promoters: Jana Holdings Ltd (JHL) + Jana Capital Ltd (JCL) — hold 16.9% (peak 44%); TVS Motors incoming strategic investor (last 4.99% + part of capital raise, pending RBI approval)
profile.mgmt: Ajay Kanwal (MD & CEO); Krishnan Subramania Raman / K.S. Raman (Executive Director); Abhilash Sandur (CFO). Moderator: Chintan Shah (ICICI Securities)
profile.subseg: Secured: Affordable Housing, MSME/MSE, Vehicle Loans (incl. Used Car, Two-Wheeler), Gold Loans, Micro LAP; Unsecured: Microfinance (MFI); Liabilities: CASA + Retail/Bulk Term Deposits

deepdive.sec: Financial Services / Small Finance Bank (secured-lending transition)

bull_bear.body: Capital raise total Rs 728 cr: Rs 103 cr received, ~Rs 80 cr pending TVS RBI approval, balance 75% staged over 18 months. Promoters (JHL/JCL) have not funded the bank since June-2022 (diluting from 44% → 16.9%); bank self-funds via IPO/private investors. Guarantee commission (Rs 80–100 cr/yr) is a deliberate capital-protection spend. No buyback/dividend detail.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Promoter (JHL/JCL) "technical default":** India Ratings downgraded the holdcos after NCD holders sought a 6-month extension to sell shares. Management stresses: no cross-default, no common board members, no bank liability, CARE did not put the bank on watch. Reputational/overhang risk, not a financial one — but monitor.
- **Deposit pricing / liquidity:** April–May were tight; rates raised in June; total deposits flat QoQ — deposit growth must re-accelerate to hit 23–25% guidance (H1 catch-up needed).
- **MFI concentration:** ~27% of book; slippages improving but Q2 slippage guided flattish (with better recoveries offsetting).
- **Government CASA:** state-government deposits lost in Q4 not yet returned (bank re-empaneled; flow "started marginally," pace uncertain).
- **Macro:** Iran war / El Nino — no impact seen yet; monitored via early-warning indicators.
- **Merger speculation** in media — management declined to comment.
- **CGMFU claim timing:** Rs 65 cr claimed Q3, balance later — recovery is a timing question, not a coverage question.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, granular and unusually direct. Ajay Kanwal proactively (and at length) addressed the promoter rating downgrade "in such an obvious manner" rather than dodging, and volunteered spreadsheet-relevant nuances (Q2 slippage flattish but recoveries improving). CFO Sandur gave precise segment numbers on demand; ED Raman handled gold and macro-risk crisply. Candid on the deposit-side "work to do" in Q2 and honest on government-deposit uncertainty ("tough to predict"). Tone: post-crisis relief + measured optimism ("best year ever"), backed by data rather than hype.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The guarantee program is the real re-rating catalyst, not the PAT** — with ~80% of unsecured covered and the book heading to 80% secured, Jana is engineering away the exact tail risk (unsecured blow-ups) that caused every prior misstep. The Rs 80–100 cr commission is the "insurance premium" for earnings predictability.
- **The clean Q1 matters more than the absolute number** — management repeatedly flagged that Q1 is seasonally "a shocker" and last year's Q1 was brutal; a strong Q1 de-risks the full-year guidance.
- **Cost-of-funds tailwind is exhausted** — future NIM defense shifts to asset-mix (higher-yield gold, secured retail) and operating leverage, not cheaper liabilities.
- **NBFC-lending pullback is a quality signal** — the bank is confident enough in its own 5 product lines to shrink wholesale NBFC exposure and still hit 20%+ growth.
- **Micro LAP negative growth is self-inflicted and temporary** (DSA→direct sourcing transition), not credit stress — an important distinction for anyone modeling the book.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Tier-1 Capital of Rs. 728 crores approved via Share Warrants under the Preferential route, of which Rs. 103 crores was received in June-2026; the TVS Venu Group awaits RBI approval for a 9.99% stake.
- CRAR (after including interim profits for Q1 FY 27) at 20.2%, versus 19.4% in Q4 FY26 and 20.5% in Q1 FY26; BVPS at Rs. 449 against Rs. 424 in Q4 FY26 and Rs. 403 in Q1 FY26.
- Borrowings of Rs. 4,659 crores as at June 30, 2026 comprise Refinance of Rs. 4,262 crores, Tier-2 capital of Rs. 375 crores and Others including call of Rs. 22 crores, with fresh borrowings from Financial Institutions during the quarter of ~Rs. 300 crores.
- Credit to Deposits ratio at 97.0% in Jun-26 versus 94.6% as at 30th June 2025, and at 85.1% after adjusting for refinance availed from NABARD, SIDBI and NHB.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Gold loans:** Rs 2,678 cr, +100% YoY / +13.5% QoQ; LTV 64%, daily price feeds + margin-call mechanism; GNPA ~0.5% fully collateral-covered; adding gold headcount + 50–75 gold branches. Unfazed by recent gold-price correction.
- **MFI (unsecured):** Rs 10,240 cr, +18% YoY; 5 consecutive quarters of declining slippages; ~80% under CGMFU guarantee; targeted growth only 10–12% FY27 — stabilizing, not chasing.
- **Micro LAP:** the one deliberate Q1 "blip" — model shifting to direct sourcing (from DSA); returns to positive growth Q2.
- **NBFC term loans:** deliberately reduced/flat — own products strong enough to hit 20–22% growth without it.
- **Affordable housing / MSME(MSE) / Two-Wheeler:** all growing well; MSE flagged for a strong Q2 acceleration; affordable housing may accelerate.
- **Liabilities:** CASA +31% YoY (7.1% QoQ, RCB/IPL branding aided); retail TD +31% YoY; bulk cut 6% QoQ to lower cost of funds; 97% retail & 83% bulk deposits are 1-year+.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Guarantee-program floor on unsecured losses:** since Nov-2024 the bank pre-emptively placed ~80% of MFI under a CGMFU guarantee — Rs 196 cr of the Rs 214 cr unsecured net NPA is covered (uncovered only Rs 18 cr). This structurally caps the tail risk that historically caused every misstep (MFI/COVID). Management calls a fully-covered unsecured book + secured majority "nearly a secured bank."
- **Diversified secured franchise:** five secured product lines (affordable housing, Micro LAP, MSME, vehicle, gold) vs a single unsecured line mathematically pushes the mix toward 80% secured each year — a self-reinforcing de-risking.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position (OPTIONAL)

business.body:
> Challenges Jana specifically discussed: the JHL/JCL promoter rating downgrade, gold-price correction, and MFI-sector normalization. Mapped to listed names via our own files where resolvable; TVS Motors is named by management.

| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| "the last 4.99%, they've committed to sell to TVS Motors… strategic tie-up with TVS Motors" | **TVS Motors** (strategic investor + two-wheeler-finance tie-up) ⭐ — not resolved to a clean ticker in our concall files | Promoter holdcos JHL/JCL (diluting, downgraded) | TVS gains a captive vehicle-finance channel + bank stake; Jana gains two-wheeler flywheel; **Med** ⭐ (named by mgmt, ticker not in-file) |
| "recent correction in the gold prices… impact on portfolio growth and asset quality" | Gold-lending banks/NBFCs with low LTV (Jana LTV 64%, GNPA ~0.5%) ⭐ | High-LTV / aggressive gold lenders | Low-LTV + daily price feeds + margin calls insulate quality; disciplined lenders take share in a correction; **Low–Med** ⭐ sector-knowledge |
| MFI-sector stress normalization — "5 continuous quarters of decline in slippages… book is stabilizing" | SFBs/MFIs that survived with capital + guarantee cover (Jana ✅) | Weaker MFIs unable to absorb the cycle | Post-stress, well-capitalized players with guarantee floors consolidate; **Low–Med** ⭐ (no specific listed peer resolved in-file) |
> Other topics (deposit pricing, promoter event, product launches) are firm-specific with no external listed beneficiary to map.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Deck's stated positioning: "We continue to serve aspirational India, underserved both on deposits and loans", "We continue to increase our secured business proportion each year", and "We are creating a sustainable, predictable and long term franchise", with digital and high standards of governance and customer service described as key components of its DNA.
- Pan-India franchise of 826 Outlets with presence in 23 States and 2 UTs, 62 ATMs and 26,287 Employees; 4.7 Million Active Customers and more than 12 Million customers served since 2008.
- "Anchor Bank" strategy built around a Home Loan leading to multiple product offerings — the deck reports CASA Penetration at 99% (Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY27), Health Insurance Penetration at 91%, Pre-approved Business Loan Program at 19% and TD/RD Penetration at 19% for Q1 FY27.
- Diversification claimed on both sides of the balance sheet: "Top 3 states 37%. No concentration" on advances and "Top 3 states 35%. No concentration" on deposits.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Promoter distress] JHL and JCL, currently promoters of the Bank, have a technical default on NCD payment as they extended the tenor by 6 months to give them time to sell their stake; JHL holds 16.9% stake in the Bank from a peak of 44%, and JHL and JCL will apply for de-promoterisation to SEBI and RBI post reduction of stake to less than 9.99%.
- [Ring-fencing] The deck states JHL has not contributed any capital to the Bank since June-2022, JHL does not have any Board member on the Bank and vice versa, and there is no cross-default linkage between JSFB debt and JHL/JCL debt.
- [Rating action] The Bank has been put under "watch" by India Rating consequent to the action on JCL and JHL, however the deck describes operations as Business As Usual (BAU); CARE Ratings has retained the Rating of the Bank with no action taken.
- [FY27 guidance] Guidance for FY 2027 is GLP Growth of ~19-21%, Deposits Growth of ~23-25% and PAT Growth of 80%+.
- [Management change] Asheesh Maroo, Chief Credit Officer, is shown as "(Resigned)" in the management listing; the board and management are described as having average experience of ~29 years in financial services.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: NIM 7.5%, restored to pre-MFI-stress levels via (1) cost-of-funds decline (−60 bps YoY to 7.4%) and (2) lower slippage → reduced interest-in-suspense. Cost of funds is now near its floor (7.3–7.4% range) as deposit pricing hardened in April–May and the bank raised rates in June. Operating leverage is the next lever: opex grew only Rs 10 cr (+1.6%) QoQ against ~20% asset growth, targeting cost-to-income down to 63–65%. Note the ~Rs 80–100 cr annual guarantee-commission (1%) is now a permanent BAU cost — absorbed while still guiding 80%+ PAT growth.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** PAT Rs 155 cr (vs Rs 140 cr Q4); NIM 7.5%; cost of funds 7.4% (−60 bps YoY); credit cost 0.45% (flat); GNPA 2.24% / NNPA 0.85% / PCR 62.4%; ROA 1.4% / ROE 13.6%. Secured +29%, mix 72.8%→80% path. Gold Rs 2,678 cr (+100% YoY), MFI Rs 10,240 cr (+18% YoY, ~80% guaranteed). CASA +31% YoY; deposits flat QoQ (bulk cut 6%). Capital raise Rs 728 cr (Rs 103 cr in). Promoter JHL/JCL "technical default" ring-fenced. Guidance reiterated: loans 19–21%, deposits 23–25%, PAT +80%, C/I 63–65%, CASA ~20%, MFI 10–12%.
- _Next Q → check: deposit growth re-acceleration toward 23–25%; Credit Line on UPI + LAS launch traction; CGMFU Rs 65 cr claim in Q3; Micro LAP return to positive growth; MFI slippage vs recovery balance; government-CASA inflow pace; TVS RBI approval + next Rs 80 cr capital tranche._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Gross loan growth:** **19–21%** for FY27 (achievable from own product lines alone; NBFC term-loan book deliberately flat).
- **Deposit growth:** **23–25%** for FY27.
- **PAT growth:** **80%+** for FY27 (after absorbing Rs 80–100 cr guarantee-commission cost).
- **NIM:** steady ~**7.5%**.
- **Cost of funds:** plateau ~**7.3–7.4%** (±5 bps); further cuts "over".
- **Credit cost:** **0.45%** at minimum maintained across all remaining quarters.
- **Cost-to-income:** reduce to **63–65%** during the year (won't go below 60%).
- **CASA ratio:** target ~**20%** for the year.
- **MFI growth:** deliberately modest **10–12% YoY** (not aggressive).
- **Secured mix:** continue toward **80%** every year (from 72.8%).
- **CGMFU recovery:** claim **Rs 65 cr in Q3** (first-ever guarantee recoveries).
- **Product launches (Q2):** Credit Line on UPI goes public; Loans Against Shares (RBI-approved Rs 1 cr limit). Nostro/trade-FX setup this month; possible small FCNR(B) in Aug/Sep.
- **Branches:** 78 planned (8 new, 30 split, 40 relocations — only 7 executed); +50–75 gold-capable branches over next 2 quarters.

outlook.body:
- **Credit Line on UPI** — mass-scale small-ticket lending (consumer durables, education, medical emergencies); management has "a lot of expectations."
- **Loans Against Shares** — new wealth-management offering (RBI Rs 1 cr limit).
- **Used-car finance** — 50 → 240-city runway; currently no BT/refinance program (pure buy/sell financing) = large untapped optionality.
- **Trade FX / FCNR(B) / Nostro** — building non-resident + trade franchise.
- **TVS Motors strategic partnership** — potential two-wheeler / vehicle-finance flywheel once RBI approves.
